port_difficulty.why: Opens one file, reads one record, closes it. No arithmetic, no branches, no output. The COMP-3 field in the layout is never touched.

blast_radius.why: Writes nothing and no other unit calls it. A layout or record length break makes it fail at OPEN or READ, which is loud. Whether it sits on the nightly cycle is not visible in the tree.

units.driving_fact: Reads SPARQ.TEST.MASTER through the same LAYOUTX copybook the writer uses.

port_difficulty.why: Mechanically trivial: opens output, writes one record, closes. The care is the byte layout of the packed decimal field, and that the code never sets the record fields before the WRITE, so the bytes written depend on what the runtime leaves in the buffer.

blast_radius.why: Sole writer of the dataset PGMR reads by a shared but undocumented layout. The copybook record is 15 bytes and the JCL asks for LRECL=80. Wrong bytes are silent for any reader that does not do arithmetic on the amount. No archived output is in the tree.

units.driving_fact: Writes SPARQ.TEST.MASTER; the record layout is the only contract with the reader, and the WRITE at line 14 follows no MOVE.

port_difficulty.why: One EXEC PGM step and one DD with DISP=SHR.

blast_radius.why: Read only, so a failed run can be rerun. Its place in the nightly order is unknown because no scheduler was parsed.

units.driving_fact: Reads SPARQ.TEST.MASTER with DISP=SHR and names no DCB, so the record length comes from the catalog.

port_difficulty.why: One step. The DD carries dataset lifecycle (NEW,CATLG,DELETE), space and a DCB (RECFM=FB, LRECL=80) that the target must state on purpose.

blast_radius.why: Creates the dataset the reader consumes. DISP=NEW fails on a second run unless something outside this tree removes the dataset first. The LRECL disagrees with the 15 byte copybook record.

units.driving_fact: Allocates SPARQ.TEST.MASTER with LRECL=80 while LAYOUTX describes 15 bytes.
